4205.body:
[v4] Promote remaining pre-v4 obsoletes to error and trim obsolete enums from the ref assembly (#4195)

Fixes: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/issues/3681
Fixes: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/issues/3682

Completes the v4 deprecation pass. The SKPaint text/font subset was already
promoted to error in #3732; this finishes the remaining pre-v4 warning-only
obsoletes now that every one of them has a stable replacement:

  * GRBackendRenderTarget(int, int, int sampleCount, GRVkImageInfo) and the
    GRMtlTextureInfo overload (iOS/macOS/tvOS) -> the ctors without sampleCount
  * SKRunBuffer.GetGlyphSpan(), SKHorizontalRunBuffer/SKPositionedRunBuffer.
    GetPositionSpan(), SKRotationScaleRunBuffer.GetRotationScaleSpan()/
    SetRotationScale() -> the Glyphs / Positions properties
  * the SKPaintHinting and SKFilterQuality enums -> SKFontHinting / SKSamplingOptions

As part of the same pass we audited the bumped Skia milestone range for APIs
deprecated or removed upstream (#3682) and found no SkiaSharp wrappers that
needed new [Obsolete] warnings for this release, so none were added.

~~ Strip the now-unused enums from the reference assembly ~~

With SKPaintHinting and SKFilterQuality marked error-obsolete, every remaining
consumer is itself error-obsolete, so the enums no longer belong in the public
v4 surface. They are removed from the reference assembly (gone from IntelliSense
and uncompilable against) while staying in the implementation assembly for ABI.

The earlier approach removed the enum *types by name* via an inline Cecil
MSBuild task. That was non-deterministic — it would silently strip any future
non-obsolete consumer — and it crashed Cecil on write because the upstream
RemoveObsoleteSymbols task left orphaned get_/set_ accessor methods behind (the
C# compiler does not copy a property's [Obsolete] onto its accessors), which
also kept the enums looking "used." This replaces that workaround with
Mono.ApiTools.MSBuildTasks 0.6.0, whose RemoveObsoleteSymbols now also removes
the compiler-generated accessor methods and backing fields
(https://github.com/mattleibow/Mono.ApiTools.MSBuildTasks/pull/24). The trim is
now attribute-driven: the removal closure follows from [Obsolete(error: true)]
itself rather than a type-name match. Restore pulls 0.6.0 from the dotnet-public
mirror; no nuget.config change ships.

~~ Keep two DrawText overloads at warning ~~

SKCanvas.DrawText(text, ..., SKFont, SKPaint) (the two overloads without an
explicit SKTextAlign) are corrected from error back to warning. They were not
obsolete in the last shipped stable (v3.119.x) — they were marked error during
v4 development, skipping the deprecation-warning cycle. Per the deprecate-then-
error policy a newly-deprecated API must first ship as a warning, so they ship
as a warning in v4 and can be promoted to error in a later release.

SKMetalView (Apple) is updated to call the GRBackendRenderTarget ctor without
sampleCount, since the sampleCount overload is now an error.

4148.title: Fix SKPixmap/SKBitmap GetPixelSpan to use RowBytes for stride
4148.author: mattleibow
4148.body:
Fix SKPixmap/SKBitmap GetPixelSpan to use RowBytes for stride (#4148)

Fixes: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/issues/4137

SKPixmap.GetPixelSpan<T>(x, y) and SKBitmap.GetPixelSpan(x, y) computed
both the span length and the (x, y) offset from Width * BytesPerPixel
instead of the pixmap's actual RowBytes. For a subset created via
ExtractSubset, the real stride is larger than Width * BytesPerPixel
because the subset shares the parent's buffer, so the returned span was
too short to cover the subset and the (x, y) offset landed on the wrong
row. A 2x2 SKColor subset of a 4x4 RGBA8888 bitmap returned a span of
length 4 instead of 6, and row 1 pointed at parent-row pixels.

Compute both quantities from the actual stride:

  * length = (Height - 1) * RowBytes + Width * BytesPerPixel, which
    reaches the last valid pixel of the bottom row without reading the
    trailing row padding past the end of the (possibly shared) buffer.
  * offset = y * RowBytes + x * BytesPerPixel.

For non-subset pixmaps RowBytes == Width * BytesPerPixel, so behaviour
is unchanged. The offset is shared through a stride-aware
SKImageInfo.GetPixelBytesOffset(x, y, rowBytes) helper, and the typed
overload computes its length in element units (rowBytes / sizeof(T)) to
avoid a byte-to-element division.

Hardening surfaced during review:

  * out-of-range (x, y) throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException.
  * empty pixmaps/bitmaps and Unknown color types (BytesPerPixel <= 0)
    return an empty span before coordinate validation, preserving the
    prior behaviour.
  * the typed overload throws when a multi-row stride is not evenly
    divisible by sizeof(T); single-row (Height == 1) pixmaps are exempt
    since stride divisibility is irrelevant there.
  * all length/offset arithmetic is checked, including the (int) length
    cast in the no-argument SKBitmap.GetPixelSpan().

The unused parameterless GetPixelBytesOffset overload (no production
callers) was removed. No public signatures changed; this is a
behaviour-only fix.

Tests in SKPixmapTest and SKBitmapTest add the issue repro plus a
GetPixelSpanReturnsExactSubsetPixels theory (in both classes) that builds
an 8x6 Bgra8888 parent encoding each pixel's coordinates, extracts subsets
at several origins -- (0,0), an interior non-square rect, the top and left
edges at non-zero offsets, and the bottom-right corner -- and asserts every
subset pixel against both the span and the independent GetPixelColor/GetPixel
oracle, with each case requiring RowBytes > Width * BytesPerPixel. Further
cases cover single-row, empty, Unknown, and a high-bit-shift (F32) color
type, and the shared offset helper.

4114.title: Obsolete remaining legacy paint state-reading APIs
4114.author: mattleibow
4114.body:
Obsolete remaining legacy paint state-reading APIs (#4114)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/issues/3732
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/issues/4113
Builds on: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4068

Several public APIs on SKCanvas, SKTypeface, and SkiaSharp.HarfBuzz silently
read legacy state from SKPaint (FilterQuality, TextAlign, or the embedded
SKFont) rather than accepting explicit parameters. Consumers cannot tell from
the signature that behavior depends on mutable paint state, and the implicit
reads block eventual removal of the compat-paint shim in Phase 2 of #3732.

This marks those APIs obsolete following the same two-tier rule used in #4068:

  * Already obsolete on main → promote to [Obsolete("…", error: true)]
  * Newly obsolete (not previously marked) → [Obsolete("…")] warning

SKPaint internals:
  * GetFont() narrowed from internal to private — only reachable from
    already-obsolete members.
  * All four GetLegacy* bridge methods marked [Obsolete]. The compiler
    auto-suppresses CS0618 when the caller is itself obsolete, so no
    pragma directives are needed anywhere.

SKCanvas:
  * 4 DrawImage, 4 DrawBitmap, 3 DrawAtlas overloads (read FilterQuality)
    and 3 DrawTextOnPath overloads (read TextAlign) marked obsolete.
  * 4 new DrawBitmap(..., SKSamplingOptions, SKPaint) overloads added as
    the migration target — callers add one parameter instead of converting
    bitmaps to images.

SKTypeface:
  * 12 public glyph-query methods (CountGlyphs, GetGlyph, GetGlyphs,
    ContainsGlyph, ContainsGlyphs variants) marked obsolete. These
    internally create a throw-away SKFont; callers should use SKFont
    directly. Equivalent test coverage already exists in SKFontTest.

HarfBuzz:
  * 4 paint-only DrawShapedText and 4 paint-only Shape overloads promoted
    to error-level obsolete.
  * 4 font+paint DrawShapedText overloads (read paint.TextAlign) marked
    as warnings pointing to the SKTextAlign overloads.

Gallery samples and tests migrated to non-obsolete overloads throughout.
Tests that specifically exercise obsolete SKTypeface glyph APIs are marked
[Obsolete] themselves rather than suppressed with pragmas.

4133.title: Move native-compat gate from [ModuleInitializer] to SkiaApi cctor
4133.author: mattleibow
4133.body:
Move native-compat gate from [ModuleInitializer] to SkiaApi cctor (#4133)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4080

The singleton rework in #4080 removed the SKObject static constructor that
used to trigger SkiaSharpVersion.CheckNativeLibraryCompatible, and re-added
the check as a [ModuleInitializer]. A module initializer runs at assembly
load — before any user code — which forces an eager P/Invoke into
libSkiaSharp before a consumer can configure native-library loading
(registering a DllImportResolver / NativeLibrary.SetDllImportResolver, or
adjusting the search path). That regressed the "set up the native binary
first, then use Skia later" pattern.

Move the gate into SkiaApi's static constructor and delete
SkiaSharpModuleInitializer.cs. SkiaApi is the single internal type through
which every P/Invoke into libSkiaSharp flows, so an explicit static
constructor (which strips the type's beforefieldinit flag) makes the CLR
guarantee the check runs before the first sk_* call — on every interop
configuration (USE_DELEGATES, USE_LIBRARY_IMPORT, direct DllImport) and
every platform — without running at assembly load. This recovers the
friendly supported-version-range message for all consumers, including code
that only touches SKBitmap, SKCanvas, SKMatrix, or SKGraphics.

Why it's safe:

  * Re-entrancy: CheckNativeLibraryCompatible reaches native via
    SkiaApi.sk_version_get_milestone / sk_version_get_increment while the
    cctor is still running. The CLR's same-thread type-initializer rule
    returns the in-progress SkiaApi type without re-running the body, and
    the only static state the version path reads (the USE_DELEGATES
    Lazy<IntPtr> handle and its delegate cache) is a field initializer,
    which runs before the cctor body.
  * No #3817 regression: the cctor body touches only SkiaApi/LibraryLoader,
    never an SKObject, so it cannot reintroduce the static-initializer cycle.
  * Negligible cost: losing beforefieldinit adds a type-init readiness check
    that is masked by the P/Invoke transition itself (~0.35% on CoreCLR,
    statistically zero on Mono/net48).

Builds clean on net48, net9.0, and netstandard2.0; version, singleton-init,
and colorspace tests pass (35/35).

4128.title: Fix SKPixmap.GetPixelSpan<T>(x,y) offset using Height instead of Width
4128.author: mattleibow
4128.body:
Fix SKPixmap.GetPixelSpan<T>(x, y) row stride offset (#4128)

Fixes: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/issues/4111

The typed-access branch of `GetPixelSpan<T>(int x, int y)` computed
the span offset as `y * info.Height + x`, which is wrong for row-major
pixel layout. The correct formula is `y * info.Width + x`.

On non-square pixmaps this produced completely wrong offsets — e.g.
requesting pixel (3, 2) on a 10×5 image gave offset 13 instead of 23,
pointing to the wrong row entirely. Square pixmaps worked by coincidence
since Width == Height, which is why the bug shipped undetected since
PR #2609 introduced the overload.

The existing tests all used 3×3 (square) pixmaps, masking the defect.
Fix the formula in the implementation and in the test assertions, and
add two new tests using non-square pixmaps (10×5 and 8×3) that verify
both span length and pixel identity across all positions.

4080.title: Rework the lifecycle of singleton instances
4080.author: ramezgerges
4080.body:
Rework the lifecycle of singleton instances (#4080)

Fixes: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/issues/3817

SKFontManager.Default (and every other process-global singleton) threw on
first access in 4.147.0-preview.1.1:

    System.TypeInitializationException: ... 'SkiaSharp.SKObject' ...
     ---> 'SkiaSharp.SKTypeface' ---> System.NullReferenceException
       at SkiaSharp.SKTypeface..cctor()
       at SkiaSharp.SKTypeface.EnsureStaticInstanceAreInitialized()
       at SkiaSharp.SKObject..cctor()

The crash was a type-initializer (static constructor) cycle. SKObject..cctor
eagerly called SKColorSpace/SKData/SKFontManager/SKTypeface/SKBlender/
SKColorFilter.EnsureStaticInstanceAreInitialized(). SKTypeface..cctor in turn
reads SKFontManager.Default and SKFontStyle.Normal, which re-enter SKObject
on the same thread. The CLR returns the half-built SKObject/SKTypeface type
with null fields instead of blocking, producing the NullReferenceException —
and because a failed cctor is cached for the process lifetime, the types stay
permanently poisoned.

While fixing the cycle we found two more lifecycle hazards in the same code
paths that caused intermittent native crashes (notably an AccessViolation /
STATUS_HEAP_CORRUPTION on net48/x86 under GC pressure). All three are fixed
here.

~~ Break the static-init cycle ~~

Delete the eager SKObject..cctor singleton chaining. Each singleton is now
created lazily and per-type via LazyInitializer.EnsureInitialized on first
access (CreateSrgb, SKData.Empty, SKFontManager.Default, SKTypeface.Default,
the gamma color filters, the blend-mode blenders, the preset font styles).
No wrapper type's initialization touches another wrapper type, so the
static-initializer graph is acyclic and the #3817 re-entrancy cannot recur.

~~ Stop teardown from freeing shared native singletons ~~

The singleton wrappers previously owned their native handle (owns: true).
On teardown the finalizer / DisposeInternal drove the shared immortal Skia
static's refcount to zero, calling the C++ destructor — which free()d static
(non-heap) storage and corrupted the heap (STATUS_HEAP_CORRUPTION 0xC0000374,
surfacing as a random AccessViolation in whatever allocated next). Guarding
only the public Dispose() was not enough, because DisposeInternal and the
finalizer bypass that guard. The singletons are now wrapped dispose-protected
with owns: false / unrefExisting: false, so the wrapper never owns the handle
and there is nothing to free on ANY path (public dispose, DisposeInternal, or
finalizer). The process-global native object lives for the process lifetime.

~~ Hold wrappers alive across P/Invoke ~~

A native wrapper passed to (or used by) a native call could be collected and
finalized mid-call when nothing else rooted it — e.g. SKPathMeasure(path)
reads path.Handle, then a concurrent GC finalizes path and frees the SkPath
while sk_pathmeasure_new_with_path is still reading it. Add GC.KeepAlive for
both `this` and native-wrapper arguments across the P/Invoke boundary in
SkiaSharp, HarfBuzzSharp, Skottie, SceneGraph, and Resources, closing the
in-flight use-after-free window (worst on net48 Release under GC churn).

~~ Tests ~~

Add focused regression and concurrency coverage:

  * SKSingletonInitTest / SKSingletonConcurrencyTest — cycle-free init and
    races across the singleton getters.
  * SKHandleDictionary{Reentrancy,Reservation,StaleWrapper,DisposeProtected}
    tests — the dispose-protected / one-wrapper-per-handle invariants.
  * SKManagedStreamConcurrencyTest — managed-stream callback concurrency.
  * Pr4080UseAfterFreeTest — a GC-hammer repro for the in-flight
    use-after-free, isolated into a serialized collection.
  * A standalone SkiaSharp.Tests.SingletonInit.Console project that asserts
    pure-process, first-touch singleton init in isolation.

API and behavioral changes: none.

4084.title: Fix WinUI Projection DLL not found for .NET 9 consumers
4084.author: mattleibow
4084.body:
Fix WinUI Projection DLL not resolved for .NET 9 consumers on Windows (#4084)

Fixes: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/issues/4082

When TFMCurrent moved from net8.0 to net10.0 (in #3514), the
`NativeAssetPackageFile` entries in `SkiaSharp.NativeAssets.WinUI.csproj`
placed `SkiaSharp.Views.WinUI.Native.Projection.dll` only into:

    runtimes/win-{arch}/lib/net10.0-windows10.0.19041.0/

NuGet's TFM resolution algorithm won't serve a net10.0 runtime asset to a
net9.0 consumer — higher TFMs are not backward-compatible. .NET 9 apps hit
a `FileNotFoundException` at startup:

    Could not load file or assembly
    'SkiaSharp.Views.WinUI.Native.Projection, ...'

In v3.119.2 (TFMCurrent=net8.0) this worked because the DLL landed in
`lib/net8.0-windows.../`, which both net8 and net9 consumers could resolve.

Include the Projection DLL in both `$(WindowsTargetFrameworksCurrent)` and
`$(WindowsTargetFrameworksPrevious)` folders so NuGet serves it regardless
of whether the consuming app targets net9 or net10. The DLL itself is built

4062.title: Migrate Linux Docker builds to .NET official cross-compilation images
4062.author: mattleibow
4062.body:
Migrate Linux Docker builds to .NET official cross-compilation images (#4062)

The old per-Dockerfile approach assembled cross-compile toolchains by
hand on Debian bases: debian/11/Dockerfile pulled `gcc-cross` apt
packages and clang-13, debian/13/Dockerfile was a separate image just
to get a newer lld for riscv64/loongarch64, alpine/Dockerfile downloaded
apk.static at a pinned SHA and built up a musl sysroot under /alpine,
and bionic/Dockerfile fetched the Android NDK r26b zip from
dl.google.com. Each had its own arch case statement and its own
toolchain assumptions, and _clang-cross-common.sh tried to share what
it could.

Replace all of that with thin layers on top of the .NET infra team's
prereqs images:

    mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet-buildtools/prereqs:
        azurelinux-3.0-net10.0-cross-<arch>[-musl]
        azurelinux-3.0-net10.0-android-amd64

These already ship Clang 20 + lld built from source, a complete
sysroot per arch under /crossrootfs/<arch>/, libc++ (static) for the
arches the .NET team ships binaries for, and current security patches.
Our Dockerfiles now just add the .NET SDK, fontconfig-dev headers
extracted from SHA-pinned .debs, and a /etc/skia-env file that the
Cake build scripts source for SYSROOT_ROOT, SYSROOT_PATH, GCC_LIB_DIR,
and the toolchain triple. ~250 LOC of bespoke toolchain construction
gone; future updates ride .NET's release cadence.

  * glibc/Dockerfile covers arm, arm64, x64, riscv64, loongarch64.
    Multi-FROM stage aliases (FROM ... AS base-x64, ..., FROM
    base-${BUILD_ARCH}) hide the .NET x64→amd64 image-tag mapping
    inside the Dockerfile; callers (build-local.sh, CI YAML) only
    ever pass BUILD_ARCH. BuildKit DAG-prunes the unused stages so
    only one base image is pulled per build.
  * glibc-x86/Dockerfile is the one exception: the .NET team does
    not ship a libc++ build for linux-x86, so stage 1 builds it from
    source by mirroring the upstream amd64 prereqs Dockerfile verbatim
    except for three substitutions (ROOTFS_DIR, build-rootfs.sh arch,
    TARGET_TRIPLE). Stage 2 layers on the same SkiaSharp env as glibc/.
  * alpine/Dockerfile uses the cross-<arch>-musl variants directly,
    replacing the Debian 12 + apk.static dance entirely.
  * bionic/Dockerfile uses the android-amd64 image whose NDK is
    discovered dynamically with `find ... | sort -V | tail -1`, no
    hardcoded version string.
  * Fontconfig dev headers are SHA-256-pinned .debs extracted into
    the sysroot at image-build time, with a post-extract sanity check
    that fails fast if usr/include/fontconfig/fontconfig.h is missing
    — catches transitional empty packages like libfontconfig1-dev on
    Ubuntu 22.04+ (a previous CI failure of this PR).
  * Per-arch verifyGlibcMax in CI fails the build if a future .NET
    image bump silently raises the sysroot glibc beyond the documented
    target.

~~ C++ runtime ~~

Most .NET cross-image sysroots are Ubuntu 18.04 (bionic) with GCC 6/7,
which lacks the C++20 support Skia now requires. native/linux/build.cake
therefore switches from `-static-libstdc++ -static-libgcc` to
`-stdlib=libc++`, picking up the libc++ that ships in the image.

That libc++.a is built with `-DLIBCXX_CXX_ABI=libstdc++`, so its ABI
symbols (operator new/delete, __cxa_throw, exception type info, etc.)
are satisfied at runtime by libstdc++. native/linux-clang-cross/build.cake
adds `-Wl,--whole-archive,-lstdc++,--no-whole-archive` to provide
those symbols dynamically; the net effect is a new `libstdc++.so.6`
DT_NEEDED on every glibc and musl SkiaSharp/HarfBuzzSharp .so.

This is not a real new requirement: every Linux .NET runtime native
library (libcoreclr.so, libclrjit.so, libclrgc.so, libhostfxr.so,
libhostpolicy.so, libmscordaccore.so) already lists libstdc++.so.6 in
NEEDED on every glibc and musl RID, so any process running `dotnet`
already has it loaded. linux-bionic-* and android-* are unaffected
because the NDK ships a self-contained libc++_static.a; build.cake
re-adds `-static-libstdc++` for the bionic variant only to avoid a
libc++_shared.so runtime dep (the initial switch to -stdlib=libc++
regressed bionic before this fix landed).

Eliminating the libstdc++.so.6 dep would require building libc++/libc++abi
from source for every glibc/musl arch (extending glibc-x86's multi-stage
pattern to all other Dockerfiles, ~250 LOC + ~15 min CI per arch);
not worth it given the .NET runtime baseline.

~~ Sysroot glibc deltas ~~

The .NET cross-image sysroots use different Ubuntu/Debian releases
than the old Debian 11/13 + gcc-cross combination, so the verifyGlibcMax
targets are:

    arm64 / x64 / x86 : 2.27  (bionic 18.04, ↓ from 2.31, broader compat)
    arm               : 2.35  (jammy 22.04)
    riscv64           : 2.39  (noble 24.04)
    loongarch64       : 2.42  (debian sid)

musl/Alpine variants stay ABI-stable across musl 1.2.x. Android NDK
remains at 27.2.12479018 / API 29.

~~ Validation ~~

Extracted every CI-produced nupkg and ran readelf -d + readelf -V on
all 51 .so files across SkiaSharp/HarfBuzzSharp Linux/Android/Tizen
native packages: every arch's DT_NEEDED matches the expected set,
GLIBC max stays at or below the configured target for each RID,
musl/bionic/android binaries have zero GLIBC_ symbols, and
linux-bionic-* correctly links libc++_static.a (no libc++_shared.so
dep).

4000.title: Add HBColor struct for proper hb_color_t representation
4000.author: mattleibow
4000.body:
Add HBColor struct for proper hb_color_t representation (#4000)

HarfBuzz's `hb_color_t` uses BGRA byte ordering (0xBBGGRRAA) while
SkiaSharp's `SKColor` uses ARGB (0xAARRGGBB). The recently-added
`Face.GetPaletteColors()` returned raw `uint[]`, so users who cast
those values to `SKColor` would get every channel wrong (R↔B, G↔G
swapped positions, A↔A swapped positions).

Since the palette API shipped only in preview releases (v4.147.0-
preview.1.1 and .2.1, April 2026), the return type can still change
without breaking stable consumers.

Introduce `HBColor` — a blittable readonly struct wrapping a single
uint with correct bit-shift accessors matching HarfBuzz's native
`hb_color_get_red/green/blue/alpha` macros. Update the generator
config to map `hb_color_t` → `HBColor` directly in P/Invoke so no
manual casts are needed in the managed layer.

Add `ColorExtensions` in SkiaSharp.HarfBuzz as the bridge between
color systems: `ToSKColor()`, `ToSKColorF()`, `ToHBColor()`, and
batch `ToSKColors()`. HarfBuzz has no floating-point color type, so
the SKColorF conversions are a convenience we provide with clamping.

Key findings from the investigation:
- hb_color_get_* are pure macros (bit shifts), not real functions —
  P/Invoke to them is unnecessary overhead
- No byte-order swapping concerns; bit positions are fixed
- No float color type exists in HarfBuzz (even COLRv1 paint API
  uses hb_color_t for all colors)

3835.title: Fix CI: samples, Docker, NanoServer, coverlet, and build chain
3835.author: mattleibow
3835.body:
Fix CI: samples, Docker, NanoServer, coverlet, and build chain (#3835)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/issues/3842
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/issues/3945
Context: https://github.com/mono/skia/pull/232

Multiple CI failures had accumulated across Tests, Samples, and Docker
stages. This PR fixes seven distinct issues to bring the pipeline fully
green on all platforms.

~~ Samples build chain ~~

The samples Cake task depended on libs → externals → externals-native,
causing the CI Samples stage to rebuild all native libraries from source
instead of using the pre-built NuGet packages from the Package stage.
This produced zlib SIMD compilation errors and Android NDK failures on
every Samples run. Removed the dependency so --target=samples goes
directly to samples.cake. Also exposed samples-prepare and samples-run
as pass-through targets.

~~ Docker samples ~~

The Windows Dockerfiles used nanoserver-ltsc2025, incompatible with the
CI agent OS (Server 2022 / build 20348):

    a Windows version 10.0.26100-based image is incompatible with a
    10.0.20348 host

Downgraded to nanoserver-ltsc2022. DockerConsole also used Linux-style
volume mount paths (/tmp/output) for Windows nanoserver containers:

    docker: Error response from daemon: invalid volume specification:
    'D:\a\1\s\...\DockerConsole:/tmp/output'

Now uses C:\output on Windows, /tmp/output on Linux. Both scripts add
$ErrorActionPreference='Stop', $LASTEXITCODE checks, and throw on
failure so the Cake runner detects Docker errors. DockerWebApi captures
docker logs on failure for diagnostics.

~~ NanoServer font manager crash ~~

NanoServer has no DirectWrite, GDI, or font support, but
sk_fontmgr_create_default unconditionally created a DirectWrite font
manager on all Windows builds. This crashed with AccessViolation
(0xC0000005) at sk_fontmgr_legacy_create_typeface during SKTypeface
static initialization — the first time any SkiaSharp code ran:

    Fatal error.
    0xC0000005
       at SkiaSharp.SkiaApi.sk_fontmgr_legacy_create_typeface(...)
       at SkiaSharp.SKTypeface..cctor()

Fixed in companion PR mono/skia#232 by returning SkFontMgr::RefEmpty()
when SK_BUILD_FOR_NANOSERVER is defined, plus null guards on
sk_fontmgr_legacy_create_typeface.

~~ SKPathBuilder migration ~~

Migrated 12 Basic Drawing samples and 1 SkiaFiddle sample from obsolete
SKPath.MoveTo/LineTo/Close (CS0618 warnings treated as errors) to
SKPathBuilder. Uses Detach() for completed strokes and Snapshot() for
in-progress rendering during paint.

~~ Coverlet bump (6.0.0 → 10.0.0) ~~

coverlet.msbuild 6.0.0 crashed with "Unable to read beyond the end of
the stream" during CalculateCoverage on macOS .NET 10. Version 10.0.0

3772.title: Add SKStream.GetData() for zero-copy stream-to-data conversion
3772.author: mattleibow
3772.body:
Add SKStream.GetData() for zero-copy stream-to-data conversion (#3772)

Fixes: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/issues/3769
Changes: https://github.com/mono/skia/pull/200, https://github.com/mono/skia/pull/211

Skia added a virtual `SkStream::getData()` in m124 (March 2024) that
returns the stream's contents as `sk_sp<SkData>` when cheaply available.
SkMemoryStream returns its backing data directly with no copy; all other
stream types return nullptr. Skia's codec and font pipelines already use
this as a fast path — SkCodec, SkPngCodec, SkWuffsCodec, and the
Fontations typeface/scanner all call getData() to avoid reading and
copying when the source is already memory-backed.

Expose this through a new C API function (`sk_stream_get_data`) and a
public `SKStream.GetData()` method returning `SKData?`. The return value
is ref-counted: `GetOrAddObject` deduplicates against any existing C#
wrapper for the same native handle, so the returned SKData survives
disposal of the originating stream.

No managed stream callback is needed — SkManagedStream inherits the base
nullptr default, which is the correct semantic since .NET streams don't
cheaply expose their contents as native SkData.

3796.title: Fix finalizer crash in SKPath when SKPathBuilder is collected first
3796.author: ramezgerges
3796.body:
Repro from a downstream app on 3.119: the finalizer thread crashed in
sk_pathbuilder_detach_path with this stack:

    SkiaApi.sk_pathbuilder_detach_path(IntPtr)
    SKPath.FlushBuilder()
    SKPath.get_Handle()
    SKNativeObject.Dispose(Boolean)
    SKObject.Dispose(Boolean)
    SKPath.Dispose(Boolean)
    SKNativeObject.Finalize()

SKPath holds a private SKPathBuilder for batched mutations and overrides
Handle to flush pending mutations on every read. SKPathBuilder is itself
an SKObject with its own finalizer and the CLR makes no guarantee about
finalization order — when the builder finalizes first, its native
pathbuilder is freed and its Handle is set to IntPtr.Zero. The path's
finalizer then runs SKNativeObject.Dispose(false), which reads Handle
on line 269 to check `!= IntPtr.Zero`. That dispatches into our
overridden getter, FlushBuilder calls
sk_pathbuilder_detach_path(_builder.Handle), and the C side dereferences
nullptr (or a dangling pointer if the same address was reallocated).

Skip FlushBuilder once disposal has begun. The pending builder mutations
are about to be discarded along with the path either way, and
DisposeNative still cleans up _builder defensively (the CAS in
SKNativeObject.Dispose makes a second Dispose a no-op if the builder
already finalized).

Added a regression test that deterministically reproduces the crash
without the fix (Test host process crashed) and passes with it.

3798.author: mattleibow

Fix Apple platform TFMs: use 26.0 for libraries, unversioned for apps (#3798)

Fixes: #3514 (regression)

The .NET 10 upgrade in #3514 set the Apple Target Platform Versions to
26.2 (matching the CI's Xcode version) instead of 26.0 (the base Xcode 26
unified SDK version). This caused library NuGet packages to ship with
TFMs like `net10.0-ios26.2`, forcing consumers to install Xcode 26.2
rather than accepting any 26.x workload.

The same PR also accidentally added explicit TPVs to the
`MauiTargetFrameworksApp` properties, which were originally introduced
in 40b0f57852 with no TPV so that apps pick up whatever workload is
installed on the build machine.

The fix splits the versioning strategy:

  * Libraries pin to the `.0` TPV (`net10.0-ios26.0`) for maximum
    compatibility — consumers need only the base workload.
  * Apps (test devices, samples) use unversioned TFMs (`net10.0-ios`)
    so they build against whatever Xcode is on the CI agent or dev
    machine, avoiding SDK/Xcode version mismatches.

Files changed:

  * `source/SkiaSharp.Build.props` — Apple TPVs 26.2 → 26.0;
    `MauiTargetFrameworksApp` restored to unversioned
  * `build.cake` — test task TFMs to unversioned
  * `scripts/VERSIONS.txt` — ref pack names and versions to 26.0
  * `scripts/cake/UpdateDocs.cake` — ref pack package names to 26.0

Verified: all 15 Apple-platform NuGet packages contain `26.0` TFMs.
iOS and Mac Catalyst CI tests pass with Xcode 26.2 installed.

3785.title: [samples] Fix Skottie package downgrade NU1605 in Uno gallery
3785.author: ramezgerges
3785.body:
* [samples] Fix Skottie package downgrade NU1605 in Uno gallery

After bumping SkiaSharp to 4.147.0, the generated samples flow
(`dotnet cake --target=samples-generate`) fails restore on
`output/samples/Gallery/Uno/SkiaSharpSample.Uno.csproj` with:

    Error NU1605: Detected package downgrade: SkiaSharp.Skottie from
    4.147.0 to 3.119.2.
      SkiaSharpSample.Uno -> SkiaSharpSample.Shared -> SkiaSharp.Skottie (>= 4.147.0)
      SkiaSharpSample.Uno -> SkiaSharp.Skottie (>= 3.119.2)

`SkiaSharpSample.Shared` brings in Skottie 4.147.0 (its in-tree
ProjectReference is rewritten to a PackageReference 4.147.0 by
samples-generate). The Uno gallery csproj has no direct Skottie ref;
the only "near" Skottie in its closure comes from Uno.WinUI.Lottie at
3.119.2, which NuGet's resolver flags as a downgrade against the
deeper 4.147.0 ask from Shared.

The targets file is the right place to declare the Skottie
ProjectReference (matching the SkiaSharp / HarfBuzzSharp pattern), but
samples-generate strips imports of `samples/_UnoPlatformSamples.targets`
along with the file itself — so a PackageReference there alone would
not propagate to the generated csproj. The direct PackageReference in
the gallery csproj is what actually fixes the generated build:
samples-generate's version-substitution bumps it to whatever's in
VERSIONS.txt, putting the floor at 4.x and shadowing Lottie's
transitive 3.x.

Two changes:
- `samples/_UnoPlatformSamples.targets`: add the in-tree
  `SkiaSharp.Skottie` ProjectReference next to the existing
  SkiaSharp / HarfBuzzSharp ones.
- `samples/Gallery/Uno/SkiaSharpSample.Uno.csproj`: pin Skottie with
  `ExcludeAssets="all"` so the package only constrains the version
  floor; the actual Skottie code keeps coming from Shared (in the
  generated build) or the in-tree project ref via the targets file
  (in the local build). A duplicate PackageReference here AND in the
  targets file trips NU1504 (and Uno.Implicit.Packages chokes on it),
  so the targets file holds only the ProjectReference.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [samples] Migrate FillPathSample to SKPathBuilder

The shared gallery's FillPathSample built its shapes with mutating
SKPath methods (MoveTo/LineTo/AddRoundRect/AddCircle/Close), all of
which were marked [Obsolete("Use SKPathBuilder instead.")] when
SkiaSharp landed at 4.147.0. SkiaSharpSample.Shared has
TreatWarningsAsErrors=true, so the gallery and SkiaFiddle Uno builds
fail with CS0618 in CI:

    error CS0618: 'SKPath.MoveTo(float, float)' is obsolete: 'Use
    SKPathBuilder instead.'
    error CS0618: 'SKPath.AddRoundRect(SKRoundRect, SKPathDirection)'
    is obsolete: 'Use SKPathBuilder instead.'
    ...

Rewrite the five Create*Path helpers to construct an SKPathBuilder,
configure it via the same MoveTo/LineTo/AddCircle/AddRoundRect/Close
calls (those methods are still supported on the builder), and call
Detach() to materialize the SKPath returned to the caller. The
builder is `using`-disposed; the caller owns the detached path
exactly as before.

FillPathSample is the only sample that still uses the obsolete
mutating SKPath methods directly — every other sample in
samples/Gallery/Shared/Samples/ already uses SKPathBuilder.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [samples] Mute NuGet WebAssembly native asset packages

The Uno wasm build was linking three copies of libSkiaSharp.a (in-tree st,
NuGet st, NuGet st,simd), producing duplicate-symbol errors across libpng,
libwebp and friends.

SkiaSharp.NativeAssets.WebAssembly's targets file adds both st and st,simd
variants to the wasm-ld command unconditionally. Listing the package as a
direct PackageReference with ExcludeAssets="all" mutes both — the in-tree
output/native/wasm/libSkiaSharp.a Content glob in IncludeNativeAssets.SkiaSharp.targets
remains the sole source. Same treatment for HarfBuzzSharp.NativeAssets.WebAssembly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [binding] Pin Uno wasm libSkiaSharp.a glob to a single variant

The in-tree Uno glob was libSkiaSharp.a/**/*.a, which would link both st
and st,simd if the native build ever produced both. Mirror the Blazor
block's _SkiaSharpNativeBinaryType computation (driven by WasmEnableThreads
and WasmEnableSIMD) and pin the variant directory in the Content glob so
WasmEnableSIMD=false actually selects what the SkiaFiddle README claims it
selects. Same change in IncludeNativeAssets.HarfBuzzSharp.targets.

Add variable font support to SkiaSharp and HarfBuzzSharp (#3703)

Changes: https://github.com/mono/skia/pull/185

typeface cloning at specific design coordinates, and full HarfBuzz
variation APIs. Variable fonts (e.g. Inter, Roboto Flex) expose
continuous design axes like weight, width, and optical size — this PR
lets consumers query and manipulate those axes from managed code.

~~ SKTypeface ~~

  * VariationDesignParameters / GetVariationDesignParameters(Span<>)
    — query axis metadata (tag, min, default, max, isHidden)
  * VariationDesignPosition / GetVariationDesignPosition(Span<>)
    — query the current axis coordinate values
  * Clone(ReadOnlySpan<SKFontVariationPositionCoordinate>)
    — create a typeface at a specific design position
  * Clone(SKFontArguments)
    — full control over position and collection index

~~ New types ~~

  * SKFourByteTag — four-byte tag struct with Parse/ToString, implicit
    uint conversion, and char constructor (matches HarfBuzzSharp.Tag)
  * SKFontVariationAxis — generated struct: Tag, Min, Default, Max,
    IsHidden
  * SKFontVariationPositionCoordinate — generated struct: Axis + Value
  * SKFontArguments — ref struct accepting spans, arrays, or stackalloc

~~ HarfBuzzSharp.Face ~~

  * HasVariationData, VariationAxisCount, VariationAxisInfos
  * TryFindVariationAxis(Tag, out info)
  * NamedInstanceCount, named instance design coords and name lookups

~~ HarfBuzzSharp.Font ~~

  * SetVariations, SetVariationCoordsDesign, SetVariationCoordsNormalized
  * VariationCoordsNormalized property and Span overload
  * SetVariationNamedInstance

Every property has a matching Span overload for allocation-free use via
stackalloc. Input validation (negative instance indices, null checks)
throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException or ArgumentNullException at the
managed boundary.

Includes 151 tests covering axis values, tag round-trips, span/property
equivalence, static font graceful handling, clone + render verification,

3745.title: Update devcontainers: split into managed and native configs
3745.author: mattleibow
3745.body:
Update devcontainers with managed/native split and fix GLIBC verification (#3745)

The old devcontainer used a .NET 7.0 image, ran setup commands in
parallel without dependency ordering, and lacked the Android workload
and SDK needed to build the test solution. Native contributors had no
devcontainer at all.

~~ Two devcontainer configurations ~~

Split into managed-only (root `.devcontainer/`, the Codespaces default)
and full native + managed (`.devcontainer/native/`). Both use
`mcr.microsoft.com/devcontainers/dotnet:10.0` to match the SDK pinned
in global.json.

  * Managed: downloads pre-built natives, installs Android workload and
    SDK, builds the test solution — ready for C# binding work.
  * Native: adds clang, ninja, python3, libfontconfig1-dev, inits
    submodules, and compiles Skia from source — for C/C++ native work.

~~ Parallelized init scripts ~~

Each config runs a single `init.sh` that backgrounds independent setup
steps (apt packages, `dotnet workload install android`, Android SDK
install via `scripts/install-android-sdk.ps1`, `dotnet tool restore`,
submodule init) then waits before running the sequential build chain.

The `dotnet workload install` uses `TMPDIR=/var/tmp` to avoid the 3.9 GB
tmpfs mounted at `/tmp` in Docker containers, which is too small for
the Android workload packs.

~~ GLIBC verification made explicit ~~

The default `verifyGlibcMax` in `native/linux/build.cake` was hardcoded
to `2.28`, which fails on modern distros (Ubuntu Noble ships glibc 2.38).
Change the default to empty (no check) so dev builds succeed anywhere,
and make CI and local Docker builds pass the limit explicitly:

  * CI pipeline: `--verifyGlibcMax=2.28` for Debian 10 matrix entries,
    `--verifyGlibcMax=2.38` for Debian 13 (loongarch64) — unchanged.
  * `_clang-cross-common.sh`: match on Docker image path instead of
    architecture so both Debian 10 (`2.28`) and Debian 13 (`2.38`) get
    the correct limit in local builds.
  * Alpine and Bionic use musl / NDK respectively — no glibc check.

~~ Other fixes ~~

  * `contrib` → `multiverse` (Ubuntu, not Debian)
  * `ttf-ancient-fonts` → `fonts-ancient-scripts` (renamed in Noble)
  * Auto-accept MS fonts EULA via `debconf-set-selections`
  * `containerEnv` sets `ANDROID_HOME`, `ANDROID_SDK_ROOT`, `CC`, `CXX`
  * Lockfiles generated via `devcontainer upgrade` for reproducibility

3730.title: Fix #3693: move default-typeface resolution to the managed layer
3730.author: ramezgerges
3730.body:
Fix #3693: move default-typeface resolution to the managed layer

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/issues/3693
Changes: https://github.com/mono/skia/compare/4db5aa5668...e6736d19f2

SkiaSharp crashed with SIGSEGV in sk_typeface_ref_default() on Android
API 36 during static initialization. The native SkTypeface::RefDefault()
path dereferenced a null pointer because the Android font manager could
not construct a default typeface at that point in startup.

Move default typeface resolution from removed Skia C++ APIs
(RefDefault/MakeDefault/MakeFromName — all deleted in m132) to the
managed layer using the font manager directly:

~~ SKTypeface.Default ~~

Use sk_fontmgr_legacy_create_typeface(null) which routes through
SkFontMgr::legacyMakeTypeface. On Android this uses fDefaultStyleSet
(searches "sans-serif", "Roboto", falls back to style set 0) — always
finds a real font. Falls back to sk_typeface_create_empty() as a last
resort. matchFamilyStyle(null) was tried first but fails on Android/NDK
because onMatchFamily(null) returns null immediately.

~~ SKTypeface.Empty / IsEmpty ~~

New public API: SKTypeface.Empty returns the SkEmptyTypeface singleton
(0 glyphs, draws nothing). SKTypeface.IsEmpty checks GlyphCount == 0,
which covers both the empty singleton and corrupt/minimal fonts.

~~ SKFont(null) — let C++ handle it ~~

Skia m132 changed SkFont to eagerly set MakeEmpty() for null typefaces
(removed the old getTypefaceOrDefault lazy resolution). The constructor
now passes null through to C++ instead of forcing SKTypeface.Default.
The font.Typeface getter returns the empty typeface via the C API —
never null in m132.

~~ SKPaint() — initialize with Default ~~

SkCompatPaint changed from SkFont() to SkFont(MakeEmpty()) in m132.
SKPaint() now initializes with a static defaultFont backed by
SKTypeface.Default so text measurement works out of the box.
Reset() uses the same default font. Removed sk_compatpaint_new();
sk_compatpaint_reset() now takes a font parameter.

~~ FromFamilyName / FromFile / FromStream / FromData ~~

Delegate to SKFontManager.Default methods. FromFamilyName uses
MatchFamily() ?? Default, making Android consistent with other
platforms (previously only Android returned null for missing fonts).

~~ Removed C APIs ~~

sk_font_new, sk_typeface_ref_default, sk_typeface_create_default,
sk_typeface_create_from_name, sk_typeface_create_from_file,
sk_typeface_create_from_stream, sk_typeface_create_from_data,
sk_fontmgr_ref_default — all removed (underlying C++ APIs deleted
in m132). Added sk_typeface_create_empty, sk_fontmgr_create_default,
sk_fontmgr_legacy_create_typeface.

~~ Tests ~~

26 new tests across SKTypefaceTest, SKFontTest, SKFontManagerTest,
and SKPaintTest covering: Empty/IsEmpty, default resolution,
FromFamilyName null/missing/empty, font constructor null handling,
paint default typeface, ZeroGlyphs.ttf test font. Updated 18
existing SKFontTest tests to use SKFont(SKTypeface.Default) for
text measurement (new SKFont() gets empty typeface in m132).

Android API 36: 3405 passed, 0 failed

3714.title: Bump SkiaSharpGenerator to CppAst 0.21.4 and make it work on Linux
3714.author: ramezgerges
3714.body:
Bump SkiaSharpGenerator to CppAst 0.21.4 and make it work on Linux (#3714)

Context: https://github.com/mono/skia/pull/186
Changes: https://github.com/mono/skia/compare/0c28aa73be...bc1f05a1bb

The generator was pinned to CppAst 0.13.0 (2021), which transitively
required libclang 15 and libtinfo5. Ubuntu 24.04+ dropped libtinfo5,
making the generator unrunnable on modern Linux without a compat shim.
The macOS-only include-path discovery also left Linux contributors
unable to parse the Skia headers at all.

Bump CppAst to 0.21.4 (libclang 18.1.0, no ncurses dependency). Three
adjustments keep the regenerated output compatible with what 0.13
produced:

  * Strip `const` as suffix as well as prefix and collapse the space
    before `*`/`&` that newer CppAst inserts, so opaque-handle lookups
    in the skiaTypes dictionary still match.

  * Reject platform-dependent C `long` / `unsigned long` outright
    instead of silently mapping them. CppAst 0.13 conflated `long` with
    `int` (giving Int32 on both); 0.21 reports `long` faithfully, which
    would otherwise pick Int64 and break the Windows ABI where C `long`
    is 32-bit. The generator now fails with a message pointing at
    int32_t / int64_t.

  * Normalize CppAst's ToString() in `// extern` and `// typedef`
    comments back to `const T*` style for cosmetic parity.

On the native side, the two remaining uses of C `long` in the Skia
C API — `sk_stream_move` and `sk_managedstream_move_proc` — are narrowed
to `int32_t` (mono/skia#186). This fixes a real bug on LP64 targets
where the .NET marshaller zero-extended the 32-bit managed value into a
64-bit register, turning negative offsets like -1 into 0x00000000FFFFFFFF.

The managed `SKStream.Move(long)` overload is marked `[Obsolete]` and
switched from silent truncation to `checked((int)offset)` so callers
get an OverflowException instead of silent data corruption.

A Linux branch is added to the include-path discovery that invokes
`clang -print-resource-dir` for built-in headers and adds the standard
system include directories.

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/discussions/3205
Fixes: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/issues/3206

Android uses the Bionic libc rather than glibc or musl, so the existing Linux
native asset packages did not cover that environment. This change adds a
dedicated `linux-bionic` runtime flavor for x64 and arm64, and wires it through
the SkiaSharp and HarfBuzzSharp packaging so those binaries can be restored and

folds pthread support into libc.

produce the new assets reliably on both supported architectures. The Bionic jobs
are handled explicitly in the Linux pipeline so they do not inherit the generic
fontconfig expectations from the glibc builds, and the NoDependencies package

3076.title: [Android] Fix SKGLView not rendering after tab switch in MAUI TabBar
3076.author: SimonvBez
3076.body:
[Android] Fix SKGLView not rendering after tab switch in MAUI TabBar (#3076)

Fixes: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/issues/2550
Fixes: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/issues/2445

An `SKGLView` placed inside a MAUI `TabBar` renders correctly on first
display but goes blank when the user switches to another tab and back.
The same symptom occurs when navigating away from a page containing an
`SKGLView` and then returning.

The root cause is in `GLTextureView.OnAttachedToWindow()`. When the view
is reattached, a new `GLThread` is created with `width = 0` and
`height = 0`. The thread expects `OnLayoutChange()` to supply the real
dimensions, but Android does not fire that callback when the view is
reattached at the same size — the layout hasn't changed, so there is no
event. The GL surface is created at 0×0 and nothing is drawn.

Pass the current `Width` and `Height` of the `GLTextureView` into the
`GLThread` constructor so it starts with the correct dimensions
immediately. When the view appears for the first time, both values are
still 0, matching the previous default, so first-display behavior is
unchanged.

3560.title: Bump SkiaSharp to Skia milestone 132
3560.author: ramezgerges
3560.body:
Bump SkiaSharp to Skia milestone 132 (#3560)

Context: https://github.com/mono/skia/pull/171
Changes: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/3560/files
AI review report: https://gistcdn.githack.com/mattleibow/b1c57a78d86cc5dec3fff1182de48f01/raw/295bb903e36917d3faf80f74ba4d3ab06adcb6ec/171.html

Update SkiaSharp from Skia m119 to m132 — the managed-side companion
to the native Skia bump merged in mono/skia#171. This moves the
assembly version from 3.119.x to 3.132.0, the native soname from
119.0.0 to 132.0.0, and all NuGet package versions from 3.119.4 to
3.132.0.

~~ Why take this bump ~~

Between m119 and m132, upstream Skia gained improvements that flow
directly through to SkiaSharp users: more consistent EXIF/orientation
handling in image codecs, HDR and wide-gamut pipeline improvements,
newer color-aware filters and drop-shadows, and accumulated
raster/perlin/filter correctness fixes. This also unblocks exposing
newer Skia APIs in future releases.

~~ New API surface ~~

SKColorType gains two values for upstream HDR color types:

  * Bgra10101010XR = 25
  * RgbF16F16F16x = 26

These are wired through EnumMappings, the bytes-per-pixel and
shift-per-pixel tables in Definitions.cs, the alpha-type validation
logic, and the GL sized-format mapping in GRDefinitions.cs.

~~ Struct ABI changes ~~

  * SKJpegEncoderOptions: now includes fOrigin / fHasOrigin fields
    matching the upstream EXIF orientation support added in m132.
  * GRVkBackendContextNative and GrVkYcbcrConversionInfo: updated
    to match upstream Vulkan shape changes.

~~ Generated bindings ~~

SkiaApi.generated.cs was regenerated to match the updated C API
(174 lines changed). This includes the new color type enum values,
the Vulkan struct layout changes, and adjusted P/Invoke signatures.

~~ Native build scripts ~~

Removed skia_use_sfntly=false from all 8 platform build.cake files
(Android, iOS, Linux, macOS, Tizen, tvOS, WASM, Windows). sfntly was
removed from upstream Skia between m119 and m132; the flag is now
unrecognized.

Added GIT_SYNC_DEPS_SKIP_EMSDK=1 environment variable passthrough
in native-shared.cake's RunPython helper so that git-sync-deps does
not attempt to activate emsdk during non-WASM builds.

~~ Submodule and branch tracking ~~

  * externals/skia now points to e2260f39c4 on the skiasharp branch
    (post mono/skia#171 merge).
  * .gitmodules branch updated from xamarin-mobile-bindings to
    skiasharp, reflecting the consolidated branch name used by
    the mono/skia fork going forward.

~~ Test updates ~~

  * New m132 color types added to EnumMappingsTest and
    ToGlSizedFormat unknown-format assertions.
  * SKImage: updated refcount expectation after FromEncodedData
    (3 → 2, matching m132 internal refcount change).
  * SKColorSpace: switched to Assert.InRange for non-deterministic
    refcounts from peek.Info.
  * SKPaint/SKFont: handle woff2 typefaces returning non-null with
    empty FamilyName under m132.
  * SKBitmap: skip Bgra10101010Xr in copy tests (unsupported pixel
    color readback on current test platforms).
  * Gray8: corrected luminance values to 0x35/0x23 matching actual
    m132 HIGHP raster pipeline output.
  * GRContext: added null-check guard for Vulkan backend test.

~~ Other changes ~~

  * LoongArch Linux build mapping: loongarch64 → loong64 to match
    Skia GN's expected target_cpu.
  * VERSIONS.txt, azure-templates-variables.yml, and
